input.quote: 3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
input.rationale: The Fees; Payment article (Section 3) imposes no minimum purchase, minimum spend, guaranteed volume or take-or-pay obligation on the Company. Our only payment obligation is a purely variable revenue share — thirty percent of Net Sales actually generated from sales of Deerskin Products on the Site, and only on Net Sales above an $11,000 monthly floor, with quarterly reconciliation for refunds and exchanges (Sections 3.1–3.3). Fees therefore accrue solely by reference to actual usage/sales, which satisfies the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage only). No volume caps or restrictions on the Company's usage appear anywhere in the Agreement, and the one-year term auto-renews subject to either Party's ninety (90) days' termination notice (Section 4.1), so there is no multi-year take-or-pay exposure. Noted for completeness, not as a deviation under this rule: Section 4.2 imposes a Termination Payment on the Company if it terminates, calculated from trailing Net Sales less $800,000 divided by two, payable in eight quarterly instalments. That is an exit-fee/liquidated-damages mechanic rather than a minimum purchase commitment (it is not triggered by any shortfall against a committed volume and cannot be avoided by buying more), and it is properly addressed under the termination/liquidated-damages rules rather than flagged twice here. Similarly, the Section 6.1 exclusivity restriction on the Company is a competitive restraint, not a volume restriction on our usage. Also HDI's own obligations to bear development, hosting and promotion costs (Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8) run in our favour.
